authoredPrompt: This figure is a labeled anatomy diagram of a horizontal ellipse, drawn as a blue outline centered at the origin of a coordinate system whose horizontal axis is marked x at the right and whose vertical axis is marked y at the top, both ending in arrowheads. A red dashed segment lies along the horizontal axis and spans the full width of the curve; the words "Major Axis" sit below its left half, and its two endpoints, where the outline meets the horizontal axis, are marked with dots and labeled "Vertex" at each end. A second red dashed segment lies along the vertical axis and spans the height of the curve, labeled "Minor Axis" beside its upper half, with black dots at its ends labeled "Co-vertex" above and "Co-vertex" below. The black dot where the two dashed segments cross is labeled "Center." Two small green dots sit on the horizontal dashed segment, one on either side of the center and well inside the vertices, each labeled "Focus." Collecting every named part on a single outline lets the reader tie each term to a definite position relative to the center. The diagram supplies the vocabulary needed to set up and read the standard equation of an ellipse.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for semi-major axis a: the learner drags the horizontal radius, the vertices and major axis stretch while the center stays fixed, and a controls the ellipse's width.
- Slider for semi-minor axis b: the learner drags the vertical radius, the co-vertices and minor axis move while the horizontal vertices stay fixed, and b controls the ellipse's height.
- Toggle between feature labels and equation parameters: the learner switches from center, vertices, co-vertices, and foci labels to a, b, and c distances, showing how the named parts map onto the standard ellipse equation.
authoredContext:
Every ellipse has two axes of symmetry. The longer axis is called the major axis, and the shorter axis is called the minor axis. Each endpoint of the major axis is the vertex of the ellipse (plural: vertices), and each endpoint of the minor axis is a co-vertex of the ellipse. The center of an ellipse is the midpoint of both the major and minor axes. The axes are perpendicular at the center. The foci always lie on the major axis, and the sum of the distances from the foci to any point on the ellipse (the constant sum) is greater than the distance between the foci. See the figure.

A horizontal ellipse centered at (0, 0) in the x y coordinate system, with Major and Minor Axes, Vertices and Co-Vertices, Foci, and Center labeled.

In this section, we restrict ellipses to those that are positioned vertically or horizontally in the coordinate plane. That is, the axes will either lie on or be parallel to the x- and y-axes. Later in the chapter, we will see ellipses that are rotated in the coordinate plane.

discrepancies: The default ellipse renders nearly circular instead of the clearly elongated 5:3 horizontal ellipse in the source, because the x and y pixel scales are unequal (xDomain spans 14 units and yDomain 9 units over a near-square plot area), vertically stretching the figure and misrepresenting the eccentricity.

The left 'Vertex' label sits above-left of the left vertex rather than to its left as in the source, and the top 'Co-vertex' sits to the right of the point rather than upper-right; minor placement drift.
The red major/minor axes read as solid red lines at inline size rather than the clearly dashed red segments of the source.
evaluation.notes: All anatomy elements (vertices, co-vertices, foci, center, dashed major/minor axes, arrowed coordinate axes) and labels are present and the a/b sliders, equation-parameter toggle, hover tooltips and click popups are genuinely functional, but unequal x/y pixel scaling makes the default a=5,b=3 ellipse look almost circular, undermining both visual fidelity to the elongated source and the pedagogical point of the reshape sliders.
action_items: Enforce an equal-aspect mapping: derive a single units-per-pixel scale (or set xDomain/yDomain ranges proportional to the actual container width/height) so that a=5, b=3 draws a properly elongated horizontal ellipse matching the source's 5:3 proportions.
Nudge the left 'Vertex' label to the left of the left vertex (anchor 'end', offset further left) and the top 'Co-vertex' to the upper-right, matching the source's label placement.
Increase the dash gap/width contrast (e.g. dasharray '7,5' with width 2.2) so the major/minor axes read as clearly dashed red at inline size.
